pass_a_gloss: [...] [Lemma, Isaiah 28:29:] Take counsel, exalt a vain comfort. Promising them the amnesty for the things on which they had acted drunkenly outrageous, and having said very well that he will not be very bitter toward them, he orders them to take hold of good counsel; and he accuses them that, having thought vain comfort to be some great and lofty thing, they are carried outside of the fitting. And what sort was the comfort among them, considered also great, but having uselessness? That one surely. For they were saying: We will make a covenant with Hades, and with death agreements; a storm rushing, if it comes upon [us], will not come to us; we set a lie as our hope, and by the lie we will be sheltered. But those pondering these things, and having the hope empty, and having thought that they will die before the terrible things, were hearing clearly: A storm rushing, if it comes upon [you], you will be for it into a trampling. When it passes by, it will take you. [Lemma, Isaiah 29:1-4:] Woe, city Ariel, which David warred against. Gather produce year upon year. For you will eat with Moab; for I will afflict Ariel, and her strength and the wealth will be [mine]. And I will encircle as David upon you; and I will cast around you a palisade, and I will set around you towers, and your words will be humbled into the earth, and into the earth your words will sink. And your voice will be like those sounding from earth, and toward the ground your voice will be weak. He takes up something of the things that happened historically in the time of the kingdom of the blessed David, and he does this all but toward showing forth of the things dared against Christ by the synagogue of the Jews. For types of the true things are the things that happened as in shadows to the more ancient. So the present Jerusalem was called Jebus once. This the blessed David besieged. And for what cause, we will know from the holy Letters themselves. For it runs thus, in the second of the Kingdoms: And David and all his men went off into Jerusalem toward the Jebusite dwelling in the land, and it was said to David that, David will not enter here; because the blind and the lame rose up, saying that, He will not enter here. And David seized the stronghold Zion; this is the city of David. And David said on that day: Let everyone striking a Jebusite attack with a dagger the blind and the lame, those warring against the soul of David. So against the blessed David the blind and lame from Jerusalem, or Jebus, stood, and having done this they perished pitiably. For he seized it; and against Christ the Saviour of all, at the time of his sojourn, the inhabitants of Jerusalem stood, lame and blind; for they did not know how to walk straight. But neither did they receive into mind the divine light, those [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: Having promised them amnesty for their drunken outrages, and having said very plainly that He will not be too harsh with them, He bids them lay hold of good counsel. But He rebukes them because they thought a vain comfort to be something great and lofty, and so were carried beyond what is reasonable. And what was this comfort which they held to be great, though it brought no profit? Surely that one. For they said: “We have made a covenant with Hades and agreements with death; if a rushing storm passes through, it will not come upon us; we have made a lie our hope, and by the lie we shall be sheltered” (Isaiah 28:15).

But those who pondered these things and held an empty hope, supposing that they would die before the calamities came, heard plainly: “If a rushing storm comes upon you, you will be trampled down by it. Whenever it passes by, it will take you” (Isaiah 28:18-19).

“Woe, city of Ariel, which David besieged! Gather produce year upon year, for you will eat with Moab. For I will afflict Ariel, and her strength and her wealth will be Mine. And I will encircle you like David, and set a palisade around you, and set towers around you; and your words will be brought low to the earth, and your words will sink into the earth. And your voice will be like those who speak from the earth, and your voice will grow faint toward the ground” (Isaiah 29:1-4).

He takes up something that happened in history in the time of the reign of blessed David, and he does this as if to bring to light what the synagogue of the Jews dared to do against Christ. For the things that befell the people of old as in shadows are types of the true things.

Now the present Jerusalem was once called Jebus. Blessed David besieged it, and for what cause we shall learn from the holy Scriptures themselves. For it runs thus in the Second Book of Samuel: “And David and all his men went to Jerusalem, to the Jebusite who inhabited the land; and it was said to David, David shall not come in here; for the blind and the lame rose up, saying, He shall not come in here. And David took the stronghold of Zion; this is the city of David. And David said on that day: Let everyone who strikes a Jebusite attack with the dagger the blind and the lame, who fight against the life of David” (2 Samuel 5:6-8).

So the blind and the lame from Jerusalem, or Jebus, opposed blessed David, and for doing this they perished miserably; for he took the city. And at the time of His coming, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, lame and blind, opposed Christ, the Savior of all; for they did not know how to walk uprightly. choices.why: God is the one promising amnesty and bidding them take good counsel; the people do not promise it.
The rebuke for prizing a vain comfort had been dropped and is restored.

choices.why: The Septuagint's Second Book of Kingdoms is the Second Book of Samuel in English Bibles.
The lame of Jebus become a figure for those who could not walk straight toward Christ.
Cyril's typological principle: events of old foreshadow the truth in Christ.
